https://www.barrons.com/articles/two-good-reasons-to-invest-in-the-u-s-1526330855 Two Good Reasons to Invest in the U.S. May 14, 2018 4:47 p.m. ET Text Size Photo: iStockphoto May 14, 2018 4:47 p.m. ET
Corporate share buybacks are on track for a record $650 billion this year, meaning more earnings per share and signifying that leaders are confident in their companies, my Barron’s colleague Andrew Bary writes . Newsletter Sign-up
Shares of companies with big buybacks have historically outperformed the market, he notes. Against the backdrop of corporate tax reform, Apple (ticker: AAPL) has a stunning, new, $100 billion program. But two other leading candidates, Alphabet (GOOGL) and Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A), remain on the sidelines.
Andrew also delves into the contentious question of whether share repurchases really buoy stock prices in the long term. “IBM (IBM) and General Electric (GE) are two prominent examples of companies that executed large buybacks at high prices and have now scaled back or eliminated those programs in the face of earnings pressures,” he notes.
Meanwhile, bond yields are sending a positive signal about the U.S. economy. Specifically, the gap between the yields on the 10-year U.S. Treasury and German government bonds is at a nearly three-decade record. It’s “a sign of investor confidence that growth remains steadier in the U.S. than Europe,” The Wall Street Journal writes .
“That spread is probably anticipating the U.S. economy is going to grow stronger than the rest of the world, and Germany in particular,” Brandywine Global Investment Management bond manager Jack McIntyre tells the Journal.
–Steve Garmhausen
